high.title: Prime Minister Le Minh Hung Directs Strong Public Investment Disbursement, Flexible Credit Management
high.summary: The government meeting focused on Q1 and April 2026 economic performance, with key monetary policy implications. Finance Minister Ngo Van Tuan reported April CPI inflation rose to 5.46% YoY (vs 3.65% in March), driven by fuel cost-push inflation affecting transportation, food services, and construction materials. The government reduced fuel taxes to 0%, leading to 8 price adjustments that decreased fuel prices 3-20.5% from end-March. However, global oil prices remained high at over $110/barrel in April. This inflation uptick is critical for SBV policy decisions and VND stability, as higher inflation typically pressures the central bank toward tighter monetary policy. The PM's directive for flexible credit management suggests continued accommodative stance despite inflation concerns, which could impact VND exchange rates and government bond yields.

high.title: MB Bank Interest Rates for May 2026: What's the Highest Rate After Recent Adjustments?
high.summary: MB Bank maintained its deposit rate structure after mid-April adjustments, with tiered rates based on deposit size. For deposits under VND 1 billion, rates range from 0.05% for demand deposits to a peak of 7.2% for 24-month terms, then declining to 7.0% for 36-60 month terms. Key medium-term rates: 12-18 months at 6.3%, 6-11 months at 4.6%. For deposits above VND 1 billion, rates are slightly higher with 24-month terms reaching 7.4%. These rates reflect competitive pressure in the banking sector and provide insight into funding costs that ultimately impact lending rates and monetary transmission. The 7.2-7.4% ceiling rates are significant benchmarks for government bond yield comparisons and indicate banks' funding pressures amid credit growth targets.

medium.title: Stock Market Enters Month with High Probability of Index Gains - Which Stock Groups Have Money-Attracting Opportunities?
medium.summary: ABS Securities analysts note historical data showing VN-Index has over 50% probability of gains in May when April rises above 5%. Vietnam's market mirrors S&P 500 patterns where strong April performance typically supports continued gains through May, countering "Sell in May" effects. This technical outlook is relevant for equity market stability and potential capital flows.

medium.title: Banks with Strongest Q1/2026 Profit Growth
medium.summary: Banking sector Q1 profits reached over VND 94,000 billion (+14% YoY) among 27 listed banks. Top performers: ABBank (+269%), PGBank (+187%), BVBank (+170%), VietinBank (+63%), VPBank (+58%). VPBank reported Q1 pre-tax profit of VND 7,900 billion (+58% YoY), driven by 33.8% growth in parent bank operations and strong credit growth. Strong banking profits support financial sector stability and suggest healthy credit demand.

medium.title: 10 Securities Companies Report "Multiple-fold" Q1 Profit Increases, One Posts Nearly 2,000% Surge
medium.summary: Securities sector showed improvement with 10 companies posting multiple-fold profit increases vs 3 in Q1/2025. Tien Phong Securities (ORS) led with 1,961% growth to VND 42 billion pre-tax profit. Strong brokerage profits indicate healthy market activity and trading volumes, supporting capital market development and investor confidence in Vietnamese equities.

medium.title: SSI Research Warns of May Correction, Reveals 9 Stocks Worth "Accumulating"
medium.summary: VN-Index surged 10.7% in April after 11% March decline, supported by global recovery and FTSE upgrade confirmation. SSI expects potential correction in May during information lull period, with Q1 results showing 20% revenue growth and 34% profit growth across the market. Banking and real estate sectors drove gains, with consumer/retail showing strong recovery signals.

medium.title: VN-Index Could Break 1,900 Points, Securities Firm Identifies Companies with Growth Potential
medium.summary: MBS Securities sees potential for VN-Index to breach 1,900 points (early 2026 peak) after 5+ weeks of recovery, though expects broad market correction as money concentrates in select stocks. Technical support seen at 1,780-1,800 points for any pullback. May represents information vacuum period that could pressure the index despite underlying strength.

medium.title: Billions of USD Preparing to Arrive, Vietnam Awaits Important June Event
medium.summary: FTSE Russell updated eligible stock list to 23 from 32 names, reducing Vietnam's weight in global indices. Vietnam's FTSE Emerging All Cap weight fell from 0.350% to 0.329%. Official list due before September 2026 FTSE GEIS review, with changes effective from August 21, 2026. Estimated $1.3 billion in ETF inflows expected from FTSE-benchmarked funds including major Vanguard ETFs.

medium.title: Over 2,700 Employees of Major Vietnamese Bank Leave Simultaneously
medium.summary: Sacombank reduced workforce by 2,736 people in Q1 to 14,080 total employees, with parent bank cutting 2,570 staff to 13,281 - lowest level in over 10 years. Q1 pre-tax profit fell 43% to VND 2,106 billion, significantly below management's earlier guidance of VND 3,572 billion. Major workforce reduction at large bank signals potential sector restructuring pressures.
